currentContext.strengths: Largest franchisee of Yum! Brands in India and Nepal, with exclusive franchise rights across key markets reinforcing competitive advantage|Disciplined expansion built on clear capital allocation principles focused on demand density, unit economics and long-term returns|Integrated multi-brand operating model creating operating leverage through shared sourcing, supply chain, distribution and overheads|Portfolio of globally loved brands plus differentiated homegrown concepts enabling participation across cuisines, occasions and consumer segments|Scale advantages in site selection, supply chain management and procurement enabling faster market expansion and cost efficiencies|Technology-led execution: omnichannel access, digital ordering, automation and AI-enabled analytics embedded across operations|Part of the RJ Corp ecosystem, providing governance foundation, entrepreneurial leadership and shared capabilities|Visionary leadership under Mr. Ravi Jaipuria with 30+ years of experience building and scaling consumer businesses, supported by a new management team led by Mr. Manish Dawar
currentContext.strategies: Transform DIL into a diversified, technology-enabled and consumer-centric multi-brand food services platform - the 'House of Brands' strategy - spanning multiple cuisines, formats, occasions and price points|Complete and integrate the proposed share-swap merger with Sapphire Foods India Limited to consolidate operations, unify marketing strategy and strengthen the supply chain across KFC and Pizza Hut, paving the way for 'DIL 2.0'|Pursue a two-track expansion approach: calibrated, cluster-based store expansion at KFC with leaner store formats, and measured re-calibration of Pizza Hut openings focused on portfolio optimisation and brand revitalisation|Increase geographic penetration across Tier II and Tier III cities in India to maximise scale and brand synergies|Scale the House of Brands portfolio through continued investment in Vaango, Biryani By Kilo, New York Fries and the newly launched Sanook Kitchen, adding multiple growth engines across consumer occasions|Adopt a data-led, digital-first marketing strategy driving hyper-personalisation through consumer insights and technology-driven campaigns, with value perception and accessibility as the core message|Differentiate the dine-in proposition to increase visit frequency and build brand loyalty, alongside smaller off-premise, delivery-led formats|Embed artificial intelligence, automation, advanced analytics and digital platforms across operations to improve customer engagement, productivity, supply chain optimisation and data-driven decision making|Grow the international business (Thailand, Nepal, Nigeria) as a demonstration of the scalability of the operating model across diverse markets|Balance growth with disciplined capital allocation, protection of unit economics and margin expansion rather than pursuing growth at any cost|Follow a 'multiplier' brand synergy approach combining the strengths of DIL and Sapphire Foods to strengthen the value proposition of Yum! Brands in India|The Company states that it did not have any Associate or Joint Venture as defined under the Act as at March 31, 2026, and governs its group structure through a board-approved 'Policy for Determination of Material Subsidiary and Governance of Subsidiaries', identifying Devyani International DMCC and Restaurants Development Co., Ltd. as its two material unlisted subsidiaries. Capital-allocation intent is expressed through a formal policy framework rather than numeric targets: the Board has adopted and periodically reviews a Dividend Distribution Policy, a Policy on Related Party Transactions (to ensure proper reporting, approval and disclosure of all related-party transactions), a Risk Management Policy and a Tax Policy, all published on the Company's website. Strategically, management frames capital allocation around disciplined, high-return deployment - the proposed merger with Sapphire Foods India Limited is expected to unlock synergies across procurement, supply chain, brand expansion and capital allocation, while the Company continues to prioritise store economics, same-store sales growth and efficiency-led margin improvement over growth at any cost.|Conducted a comprehensive double materiality assessment (in FY2024-25) to identify and prioritise ESG topics most relevant to the business and stakeholders, with each material topic mapped to associated risks and opportunities and defined action plans|BRSR disclosures externally assured by DEKRA Testing, Inspection & Certification India Private Limited - reasonable assurance for BRSR Core KPIs and limited assurance on other selected indicators|Dedicated ESG accountability at senior level: Mr. Pankaj Virmani serves as Chief Sustainability Officer & Company Secretary and is the designated BRSR contact|Food safety commitment: all critical raw materials sourced from GFSI-compliant suppliers, with stores regularly evaluated by franchisors, third-party agencies and regulators under strict SOPs from preparation to storage|Environment and Waste Management Policy driving waste reduction, segregation, timely disposal, hygiene standards and regulatory compliance|Energy management and climate action treated as an opportunity - adopting energy-efficient operations and renewable energy to reduce costs and emissions|Commitment to prudent water management and conservation practices across operations to optimise operational cost and environmental footprint|Sustainable packaging adoption to reduce demand for fresh raw materials and preserve natural resources|Human Rights and Equal Opportunity Policy backed by a grievance mechanism for fair, confidential and timely resolution of employee concerns|Diversity and inclusion: women represent 30% of the permanent employee base of 15,955 employees, with a stated focus on equal opportunity and an inclusive workplace|Employee well-being: the Company invested 6.20 crore towards employee well-being during FY 2025-26, covering financial security, healthcare support and family-friendly benefits|Menu innovation and nutrition treated as a material ESG opportunity - aligning offerings with evolving consumer health preferences|Formal, multi-stakeholder grievance redressal mechanisms in place for communities, investors, shareholders, employees and workers, customers and value-chain partners, each with a published policy or channel|Reporting boundary and scope disclosed on a standalone basis, covering operations of 1,758 stores, 15 warehouses and 1 commissary in India plus three international markets operated through subsidiaries
currentContext.expansion: DIL's expansion in FY 2025-26 was network- and platform-led rather than plant-led. As of March 31, 2026 the Company operated 2,256 stores across India, Nepal, Nigeria and Thailand, up from 2,039 a year earlier, spanning dine-in, takeaway, delivery, travel hubs and other convenience-led formats and supported by capabilities in site selection, supply chain management and procurement. Inorganically, the Company acquired Sky Gate Hospitality Private Limited during the year - discharging part of the consideration for a ~80.72% fully-diluted equity stake through a preferential allotment of equity shares - bringing Biryani by Kilo and Goila Butter Chicken into the portfolio and marking entry into the sizable and underpenetrated Indian cuisine segment, reducing dependence on global QSR formats. The defining expansion step is the proposed share-swap merger with Sapphire Foods India Limited announced on January 01, 2026: upon completion the merged entity is expected to operate over 3,000 restaurants across multiple geographies and generate approximately USD 1 billion in annual revenues, and the transaction is expected to be completed by March 2027 subject to regulatory and statutory approvals. The Company also advanced its multi-brand, multi-format transition by securing franchise rights for emerging international brands such as New York Fries and Sanook Kitchen and expanding into new categories including youth-focused snacking and Thai cuisine, aligned to the 'food-on-the-go' trend. Alongside network growth, DIL is investing in becoming a technology-enabled platform - embedding artificial intelligence, automation, advanced analytics and digital technologies to enhance customer engagement, productivity and supply-chain optimisation - while remaining focused on store economics, same-store sales growth and efficiency-led margin improvement. No public deposits were accepted and no amount was transferred to reserves during the year.
currentContext.mdna: Consumer demand in food services remained relatively subdued through much of the first three quarters as discretionary spending moderated, requiring sharper execution and greater operational discipline|The fourth quarter witnessed early signs of recovery, with improving consumption trends across several markets supported by government measures to stimulate demand and improving consumer confidence|Value-led initiatives at KFC together with continued product innovation across brands resonated with customers and contributed to improving average daily sales and a gradual stabilisation in same-store sales performance|India's foodservice market is projected to expand from approximately USD 94 billion in 2026 to USD 153 billion by 2031, a CAGR of ~10.3%, with the QSR segment growing from approximately USD 30 billion to USD 47 billion at a CAGR of ~9.3%|Structural shift from an unorganised market to an organised, branded ecosystem, with delivery-led channels, cloud kitchens and takeaway models seeing accelerated adoption on asset-light economics|Low penetration headroom: the Indian food service market is under 2% of GDP at a per-capita income of ~USD 2,800, versus the USD 7,500 threshold at which discretionary consumption globally accelerates|Digital ecosystem - smartphones, digital payments and aggregator platforms such as Zomato and Swiggy - expanding market access, order frequency and omnichannel capability|Urbanisation, nuclear and dual-income households and time-constrained lifestyles driving convenience-led, multi-daypart out-of-home consumption|Scale-driven margin levers: shared sourcing, supply chain and overheads across the multi-brand platform, plus merger synergies across procurement, technology and corporate functions|Integration of Sky Gate Hospitality progressed well, with the business achieving brand contribution break-even ahead of original expectations|Cost inflation, evolving regulatory standards and heightened competition remain headwinds operators must navigate|RBI projects India GDP growth of 6.6% for FY 2026-27, with private consumption the primary engine, supporting a favourable demand backdrop

risks.risk: Macroeconomic & market risk - discretionary demand sensitivity
risks.note: Exposure to economic slowdowns, inflationary pressures and shifts in consumer sentiment that may adversely affect discretionary spending and overall demand. Mitigated through a multi-tier pricing architecture, continuous menu innovation and value engineering to offset input-cost inflation, and ongoing monitoring of macro indicators to recalibrate pricing and promotions. Management explicitly flags that near-term uncertainties relating to consumer demand and input costs will require close monitoring.

Revenue volatility from festive cycles, regional demand patterns and evolving consumer preferences can hit store-level performance and capacity utilisation. Addressed with advanced analytics and predictive demand modelling, agile workforce and inventory planning, and targeted campaigns and product bundling to drive traffic in lean periods.

risks.risk: Operational & organizational risk - execution and key-person dependency
risks.note: Process inefficiencies, execution gaps or dependency on key personnel may disrupt operations or impact service quality across a 2,000-plus store network. Mitigated by clearly defined standardised operating procedures across locations, a strengthened governance structure with defined roles, accountability and escalation mechanisms, and leadership pipeline development with structured succession planning.

Supplier concentration, logistics constraints, geopolitical factors and commodity price volatility can affect availability and cost structures for a food business. Managed through a diversified, geographically distributed supplier network, long-term strategic sourcing agreements for cost predictability, technology-enabled supply-chain visibility with real-time inventory tracking, and periodic supplier audits and risk assessments.

risks.risk: Human capital risk in a high-attrition industry
risks.note: Attracting, retaining and upskilling talent in a high-attrition industry can impact service delivery and growth plans; the BRSR shows permanent-employee turnover remaining elevated. Mitigated by structured recruitment, onboarding and performance management, continuous investment in training and leadership development, engagement and wellness programmes with performance-linked incentives, and a focus on diversity, equity and inclusion.

As the business becomes increasingly technology-enabled - with digital ordering, kiosks, analytics and data-driven HR and supply-chain systems - risks relate to system downtime and scalability limitations, making resilience of digital platforms central to operations.

Identified in the BRSR double-materiality assessment as a material risk with negative financial implications: any compromise in food safety and quality may result in customer dissatisfaction along with regulatory scrutiny, notices and penalties. Mitigated through rigorous hygiene standards from preparation to storage under strict SOPs, regular evaluation of stores by franchisors, third-party agencies and regulators, and sourcing of all critical raw materials from GFSI-compliant suppliers.

BRSR-identified material risk with negative financial implications: inadequate waste management can result in regulatory non-compliance, and improper disposal may lead to environmental contamination of soil, water and air. Governed by the Company's Environment and Waste Management Policy covering waste reduction, segregation, timely disposal, hygiene standards and regulatory compliance.

risks.risk: Human rights and workforce grievance risk
risks.note: BRSR-identified material risk with negative financial implications: neglecting human rights results in workforce dissatisfaction, operational setbacks and reduced stakeholder confidence. Managed through a robust grievance mechanism supported by the Human Rights and Equal Opportunity Policy ensuring fair, confidential and timely resolution.

one-line thesis: Devyani delivered a strong Q4FY26 with KFC posting its best SSSG (4.9%) in 14 quarters driven by a strategic pivot to dine-in, while guiding for 200-225 net new stores in FY27. The proposed merger with Sapphire Foods remains on track for completion by FY26 end, promising scale synergies, though near-term margins face pressure from elevated coffee/cocoa costs and gas volatility.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 1,437 Cr (+18.5% YoY); EBITDA: INR 123 Cr (8.6% margin, +13.8% YoY); PAT: Not explicitly broken out in transcript text but implied via EBITDA growth; Order Book: N/A (Retail); Net Debt: Temporary increase due to Thailand equity infusion (squared off in April); One-offs: Gas crisis impact managed minimally; Intangible asset increase due to Biryani By Kilo consolidation.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Double-digit expected via volume/mix; Margin: Focus on operational leverage despite input costs; Store Inflow: 200-225 net new stores in FY27 (100-110 KFC); Capex: Tech investments within existing budgets; Commissioning: Merger with Sapphire by FY26 end.
order book & pipeline: System store count: 2,256 (Net +217 in FY26); KFC: 783 stores; Pizza Hut: 639 stores (no net adds); International: Strong growth trajectory.
segment / subsidiary detail: KFC: Rev 586 Cr (+15% YoY), SSSG +4.9%, Brand Contrib Margin 17.0%; Pizza Hut: SSSG -3.7% (sequential improvement), Brand Contrib slightly negative; Own Brands (Vaango/BBK): Mid-single digit positive SSSG, BBK turned profitable; International: Rev >500 Cr (+20% YoY), Brand Contrib Margin 17.7%; Franchise (Costa): Rev +3% YoY, GM down 1.2% due to commodity costs.
growth verticals / optionality: Merger with Sapphire Foods (USD 1B combined topline); Biryani By Kilo offline express format expansion; Travel/Highway food court expansion; Digital kiosk penetration (>80% in KFC).
margins & cost dynamics: Gross Margin 68.8% (improved YoY); Brand Contribution 14.1% (improved YoY); Headwinds: Elevated coffee/cocoa prices impacting Costa GM; Gas crisis volatility (mitigated via electrification); Tailwinds: Favorable raw material/packing costs for KFC; Shift in promo mix favoring dine-in improved KFC margins.
capex / expansion: Tech/AI overlay on existing infrastructure; No major change in store-level capex guidance; Electrical equipment conversion to mitigate gas risk.
capital allocation: Debt used temporarily for Thailand equity infusion (repaid); Intangible asset build-up from BBK consolidation; Focus on organic store expansion (200-225 stores).
risks & watch-items: Gas supply volatility; Commodity inflation (coffee/cocoa); Pizza Hut turnaround execution risk; Macro demand sustainability; Merger regulatory approval delays (CCI).
management quality / tone: Confident on KFC revival and merger timeline; Pragmatic on macro uncertainties; Transformational regarding new leadership (CTO, CMO, COO) and 'DIL 2.0' strategy.
non-obvious takeaways: Strategic decoupling of online vs. offline pricing/promotions to drive dine-in traffic (offline gains > online losses); Discontinuation of 'Tea Live' brand after testing; Shift to electrical cooking equipment in BBK to hedge gas risk; Temporary debt spike was specifically for Thailand equity, not operational stress.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Elevated coffee and cocoa prices compressing gross margins by 1.2% YoY in franchise segment. | Devyani International Ltd | loser | Med | While top-line grew 3% in Costa, input cost inflation directly hit GM; management monitoring closely but no immediate pricing fix mentioned. |
| Gas crisis volatility impacting operational costs and supply chain stability. | Devyani International Ltd | loser | Low | Management claims minimal impact due to effective handling and switch to electrical equipment, but risk remains fluid. |
| Need for aggressive store expansion to capture market share post-merger. | Devyani International Ltd | beneficiary | High | Guidance of 200-225 net new stores (100+ KFC) combined with Sapphire merger creates significant scale opportunity. |
